text:
The area (in sq. units) of the region

{(x,y) $\in$ $R^{2}$ : $x^{2}$ $\leq$ y $\leq$ 3 – 2x}, is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 8th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


$x^{2}$ $\leq$ y $\leq$ – 2x + 3

$\Rightarrow$ $x^{2}$
 = – 2x + 3

$\Rightarrow$ $x^{2}$
 + 2x – 3 = 0
 

$\Rightarrow$ (x + 3) (x – 1) = 0
 

$\Rightarrow$ x = – 3, x = 1

Area = $\int\limits _{-3}^{1}\left (-2x+3-x^{2}\right )dx$

= $\left (-x^{2}+3x-\frac{x^{3}}{3}\right )_{-3}^{1}$

= $\left (-1+3-\frac{1}{3}+9+9-9\right )$

= 11 - $\frac{1}{3}$

= $\frac{32}{3}$ sq. unit

c $\in$ (0,1), depending on ƒ, such that
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 8th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
If we consider the case where f(x) is a constant function, then its derivative f'(x) is equal to 0 for all x in the interval (0,1). 

Therefore, if we substitute this into the expressions provided in Options A, B and C, we would have :

Option A : |f(c) - f(1)| < |f'(c)| would become |constant - constant| < |0|, which is 0 < 0. This is not true.

Option B : |f(c) + f(1)| < (1 + c)|f'(c)| would become |constant + constant| < (1 + c)$\times$0, which is a positive number < 0. This is not true.

Option C : |f(c) - f(1)| < (1 - c)|f'(c)| would become |constant - constant| < (1 - c)$\times$0, which is 0 < 0. This is not true.

Hence, for the case where f(x) is a constant function, none of the options A, B and C are correct.

So, the correct answer would be Option D : None.

text:
If $A=\left (\begin{array}{ll} 2 & 2 \\ 9 & 4 \end{array}\right )$ and $I=\left (\begin{array}{ll} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{array}\right )$ then $10A^{–1}$ is
equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 8th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
According to Cayley Hamilton equation

|A – $λ$I| = 0

$\Rightarrow$ $\left |\begin{array}{ll} 2-λ & 2 \\ 9 & 4-λ \end{array}\right |$ = 0

$\Rightarrow$ (2 – $λ$)(4 – $λ$) – 18 = 0

$\Rightarrow$ 8 – 2$λ$ – 4$λ$ + $λ^{2}$
 – 18 = 0

$\Rightarrow$ $λ^{2}$
 – 6$λ$ – 10 = 0

$\therefore$ $A^{2}$
 – 6A– 10 = 0

$\Rightarrow$ $A^{–1}(A^{2}) – 6A^{–1}A – 10A^{–1} = 0$

$\Rightarrow$ $A – 6I – 10A^{–1} = 0$

$\Rightarrow$ $10A^{–1} = A – 6I$

Probability
that A or B occurs is

Doing (2) - (1)

P(A $\cap$ B) = $\frac{1}{2}-\frac{2}{5}$ = 0.10

text:
Let S be the set of all real roots of the equation,

$3^{x}(3^{x} – 1) + 2 = |3^{x} – 1| + |3^{x} – 2|$. Then S :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 8th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let $3^{x} = t$ ; t $>$ 0

t(t – 1) + 2 = |t – 1| + |t – 2|

$t^{2} – t + 2 = |t – 1| + |t – 2|$

Case-I : t $<$ 1

$t^{2} – t + 2 = 1 – t + 2 – t$

$\Rightarrow$ $t^{2} + 2 = 3 – t$

$\Rightarrow$ $t^{2} + t – 1 = 0$

$\Rightarrow$ t = $\frac{-1\pm \sqrt{5}}{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ t = $\frac{\sqrt{5}-1}{2}$ [ As t $>$ 0]

Case-II : 1 $\leq$ t $<$ 2

$\Rightarrow$ $t^{2} – t + 2 = t – 1 + 2 – t$

$\Rightarrow$ $t^{2} – t + 1 = 0$

D $<$ 0 so no real solution.

Case-III : t $\geq$ 2

$\Rightarrow$ $t^{2} – t + 2 = t – 1 + t – 2$

$\Rightarrow$ $t^{2} – 3t + 5 = 0$ 

$\Rightarrow$ D $<$ 0 so no real solution.

If $\frac{\sqrt{2}\sin α}{\sqrt{1+\cos 2α}}=\frac{1}{7}$ and $\sqrt{\frac{1-\cos 2β}{2}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}$

$α,β\in \left (0,\frac{π}{2}\right )$ then tan($α$ + 2$β$) is equal to
$_____$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 8th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\frac{\sqrt{2}\sin α}{\sqrt{1+\cos 2α}}=\frac{1}{7}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{\sqrt{2}\sin α}{\sqrt{2\cos ^{2}α}}$ = $\frac{1}{7}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{\sqrt{2}\sin α}{\sqrt{2}\cos α}$ = $\frac{1}{7}$

$\Rightarrow$ tan$α$ = $\frac{1}{7}$

Also given $\sqrt{\frac{1-\cos 2β}{2}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{\sqrt{2}\sin β}{\sqrt{2}}$ = $\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}$

$\Rightarrow$ sin $β$ = $\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}$

$\therefore$ tan $β$ = $\frac{1}{3}$

$\tan 2β=\frac{2\tan β}{1-\tan ^{2}β}$

= $\frac{2\left (\frac{1}{3}\right )}{1-\frac{1}{9}}$ = $\frac{3}{4}$

$\therefore$ tan($α$ + 2$β$) = $\frac{\tan α+\tan 2β}{1-\tan α.\tan 2β}$

= $\frac{\frac{1}{7}+\frac{3}{4}}{1-\frac{1}{7}.\frac{3}{4}}$

= $\frac{25}{25}$ = 1

text:
Let ƒ(x) be a polynomial of degree 3 such that
ƒ(–1) = 10, ƒ(1) = –6, ƒ(x) has a critical point
at x = –1 and ƒ'(x) has a critical point at x = 1.
Then ƒ(x) has a local minima at $x = _______$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 8th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let $f(x) = ax^{3}$
 $+ bx^{2}$
 + cx + d

Given f(-1) = 10, f(1) = -6

$\therefore$ -a + b - c + d = 10 ....(i)

and a + b + c + d = -6 ......(ii)

adding (i) + (ii)

2(b + d) = 4

$\Rightarrow$ b + d = 2 ....(iii)

$f'(x) = 3ax^{2} + 2bx + c$

Given f'(-1) = 0

$\Rightarrow$ 3a - 2b + c = 0 .....(iv)

f"(x) = 6ax + 2b

Given f"(1) = 0

$\therefore$ 6a + 2b = 0 ....(v)

$\Rightarrow$ b = -3a

adding (iv) + (v), we get

9a + c = 0 ....(vi)

$\Rightarrow$ $9\left (\frac{-b}{3}\right )$ + c = 0

$\Rightarrow$ c = 3b

f(x) =
$\frac{-b}{3}x^{3}$ $+ bx^{2} + 3bx + (2 - b)$

$\Rightarrow$ $f'(x) = -bx^{2}$
 + 2bx + 3b

 $= -b(x^{2}$
 - 2x - 3)

At maxima and minima f'(x) = 0

$\therefore$ $(x^{2}$
 - 2x - 3) = 0

$\Rightarrow$ (x - 3) (x + 1) = 0

x = 3, -1

As a + b + c + d = -6

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{-b}{3}$ + b + 3b + 2 - b = -6

$\Rightarrow$ b = -3

$\therefore$  $f'(x) = 3(x^{2}$
 - 2x - 3)

$\Rightarrow$ f''(x) = 3(2x
 - 2)

At x = 3, f''(x) = 3(2.3
 - 2) = 12 > 0

$\therefore$ Minima
at x = 3.

text:
The number of 4 letter words (with or without
meaning) that can be formed from the eleven
letters of the word 'EXAMINATION' is
$_______$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 8th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
2A, 2I, 2N, E, X, M, T, O

To form four letter words

Case 1 : All same ( not possible)

Case 2 : 1 different, 3 same (not possible)

Case 3 : 2 different, 2 same

$= ^{3}C_{1}$ $\times$ $^{7}C_{2}$ $\times$ $\frac{4!}{2!}$ = 756

Case 4 : 2 same of one kind, 2 same same of other kind

$= ^{3}C_{2}$ $\times$ $\frac{4!}{2!2!}$ = 18

Case 5 : All letters are different

$= ^{8}C_{4}$ $\times$ 4! = 1680

$\therefore$ Total ways = 1680 + 756 + 18 = 2454
